insights.statement: Young men feel most themselves in the quiet minutes before they walk into the room.
insights.tension: They look confident at the party, but the confidence is assembled alone, minutes before.
insights.evidence: The last look in the car mirror, the deep breath before the door.
insights.gulf_meaning: Before a wedding or a gathering, the private ritual of getting ready is part of the occasion itself.

insights.statement: A scent is felt before it is understood; people remember its texture, not its notes.
insights.tension: Nobody can name the notes, yet everyone can say how a scent feels.
insights.evidence: People describe perfume as warm, heavy or clean, never by its ingredients.
insights.gulf_meaning: In the Gulf, oud and bakhoor are described by how they fill a room, not by what they contain.

insights.statement: The things that make a man are handed down, not bought.
insights.tension: Young men want to be self-made, but the gestures that make them come from an elder.
insights.evidence: A father teaching his son to wear the ghutra, an uncle's first gift of oud.
insights.gulf_meaning: Manhood in the Gulf is passed on in the majlis, from the older generation to the younger.
